newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS - AUGUST 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS - AUGUST 14.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- ITV RECRUITS GRANADA STAR

David Liddiment, managing director of Granada UK broadcasting, has been named by ITV as its new director of programmes. Liddiment will be in charge of commissioning and scheduling all of the programmes on the ITV network, including the politically sensitive decision on whether to reschedule the flagship News At Ten programme. The appointment follows the announcement last month that Richard Eyre, chief executive of London's Capital Radio, would be ITV's first chief executive.
-- DIRECTOR QUITS ZENECA FOR RIVAL

Shares in pharmaceutical group Zeneca fell 60p to 1886.5p on Wednesday following news that a second senior executive had resigned. David U'Prichard, Zeneca's research director, left to join rivals SmithKline Beecham. The move follows the loss eight days ago of Zeneca finance director John Mayo to GEC.
-- GAS SEEKS VAT CONCESSIONS

British Gas Trading is said to be facing an uphill struggle in its bid to secure concessions from the Treasury over VAT rules which could land the company with a huge bill for customers in credit when the levy on power bills is reduced from 8 per cent to 5 per cent next month. BGT, the marketing arm of Centrica, wants to avoid following the lead of electricity companies which have opted to protect customers by paying the difference in VAT rates direct to Customs and Excise.
THE TIMES
-- LAURA ASHLEY TO HALT GROWTH IN US

Fashion and home furnishings retailer Laura Ashley is reported to be considering a halt to its expansion in the US, where it has been closing smaller stores and opening at larger sites over the past two years. The process was the cornerstone of the turnaround strategy of Ann Iverson, the company's American chief executive. Laura Ashley is also expected to announce details next week of further job losses at its Welsh factories.
-- DISPUTE ERUPTS OVER CELLNET BILLING CONTRACT

AMS, an American information technology company, has turned up the heat in a simmering contract dispute with British mobile phone company Cellnet by confirming that it would cease working on a new billing system for the UK firm. Cellnet, which claims the AMS system is already late and ridden with errors, is to take a 40m stg charge this year to cover the faulty system.
-- ENERGY TAKES 112M STG HIT ON WINDFALL TAX

Anglo-US power company Energy Group has taken a 112m stg charge to cover the UK 'windfall tax' at its Eastern Electricity subsidiary. The bill was contained in figures from the group for the three months to June, which also reported a 2 per cent dip in operating profits to 96m stg. The fall was attributed to 20m stg of seasonal losses at Energy's coal-fired power stations.
THE GUARDIAN
-- JOBLESS HITS 17-YEAR LOW

Official figures have revealed that unemployment in the UK plunged to a 17-year low in July, with the number of people out of work and seeking benefit falling by 49,800 to 1,550,000. Separately, figures from the Office for National Statistics showed that pay rises averaged 4.25 per cent over the year to July, while a forecast from the Bank of England claimed that the economy is on course to hit the government's 2.5 per cent target for retail price inflation.
-- EUROTUNNEL SALES SCARRED BY FIRE

Eurotunnel, the Anglo-French operator of the Channel tunnel, has reported a 24 per cent fall in first-half sales, to 168.8m stg. The results were badly affected by the fire in the tunnel last November, which forced its closure for several weeks. The company claimed that since the full reopening of the tunnel in June, traffic volume had almost recovered to last summer's levels, and that if the insurance payments it has received so far for the fire were included in the figures, sales would have been 221.2m stg.
-- LVMH BUBBLES ON SALES BOOM

Louis Vuitton Moet Hennessey (LVMH), the French luxury goods company, has reported booming sales for the first half of the year. Buoyed by surging demand for leather goods and champagne, the company said that sales for the three month period to the end of June rose 55 per cent, to FFr10.73bn (1.2bn stg). The figures mean that sales for the first half of the year topped FFr21.6bn, prompting a sharp rise in the LVMH shares on the Paris bourse.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- RECS WARN CONTROLS WILL DAMAGE COMPETITION

Electricity companies have warned the government that new price controls proposed by industry regulator Professor Stephen Littlechild could risk damaging moves towards domestic power competition next year. The warning was detailed in a letter from the Electricity Association to John Battle, the energy minister, and followed what had been described as 'frosty' meetings between Professor Littlechild and the regional electricity companies.
-- HOLLICK RULES OUT CABLE MERGER

United News & Media, the media conglomerate of Lord Hollick, has ruled out joining merger talks with cable operators Telewest and NTL. An alliance involving the two companies and UNM had been sought by NTL in order to create a challenger to Cable & Wireless Communications, the UK's largest cable company. Separately, NTL has announced a large restructuring of its customer operations departments, a move that will entail the loss of 50 jobs.
-- ITV PROGRAMME BUDGET LACKING

New research from investment house Merrill Lynch has suggested that ITV needs to boost its spending on programmes dramatically to avoid losing viewers to Channel 5 and satellite and cable television. The research shows that Channel 5 has eaten into ITV's audience share as the network failed to increase its programming expenditure sufficiently. Channel 4, by contrast, raised its spending on programmes by 16 per cent this year and saw its audience share increase despite the introduction of Channel 5.
